pipeline_graph.consumption_note: parse-chunks consumes semantic-chunk-plan.json + chunk-responses/ (optional --intake is used only for the write-path guard); synthesize consumes chunk-results.json (+ optional plan/intake/redaction); quality-gate consumes final-review.json + chunk-results.json (+ optional intake/plan/redaction/checks, --critical-pr). pr-brief.json and chunk-payload-manifest.json are NOT consumed downstream of build-payloads.

obligations.proposition: Every file lacking an observable textual hunk is excluded from files_covered at plan level, for all tiers, with a tier-distinct reason code.
positive_controls: same PR where the non-must file has a textual hunk remains complete/passed
obligations.discriminator: paired input differing only in presence of the @@ hunk for the non-must file
obligations.closure_predicate: RED on base, GREEN on head, observed at the gate output; mutation of the generalized predicate back to must_review-only turns the focal test RED
obligations.open_decision: whether a non-must hunk-less file degrades the plan (status) or only moves to files_not_covered with an informational code — to be fixed in the V1-C1 task contract against #232's own text ('coverage: complete' semantics). Note: the second alternative requires changing _plan_status, because any files_not_covered currently returns degraded (semantic_chunker.py:741-742).

obligations.proposition: A finding lacking a checkable negative consequence or whose cited subject is not present in the reviewed material leaves the confirmed-finding partition with a reason code, at all severities, through a channel that does not make the verdict stricter than the confirmed finding it replaces.
obligations.mechanism_site: app/agent_review/finding_normalizer.py:122-227; target channel per open_decision (NOT _downgrade_or_reject's risk channel for P3, which escalates the verdict). The only existing non-escalating channel, rejected_findings, is typed by the RejectedFindingReason Literal (schemas.py:62,341): a new reason code changes a v1 schema literal and falls under the golden-fixture constraint. Aboutness needs reviewed material as new parser input.
positive_controls: PC-CL3-01: real contract violation with concrete hunk evidence and demonstrated consequence survives at its severity
obligations.closure_predicate: each CM RED->GREEN observed on the confirmed/risk/rejected partition at synthesis and gate; no CM-CL3 case ends with a stricter verdict than before; PC-CL3-01 GREEN before and after; mutation removing each predicate turns its focal test RED
constraints: response-contract change requires positive justification against frozen v1 golden fixtures
obligations.open_decision: target channel: NormalizedRisk escalates to approve_with_required_followup; rejected_findings yields approve_with_minor_notes; v1 has no neutral observation channel
obligations.decidability_constraint: A deterministic predicate can only decide what its input material decides. Hunk text decides aboutness of symbols cited as changed; it does NOT decide absence claims about the rest of the tree (CM-CL3-03: 'setting undocumented' while documented in four other places). For each CM-CL3 case the V1-C3 contract must either supply exact-tree evidence (search of the reviewed checkout at the exact head) or exclude that case from deterministic closure and record it as an advisory-only limitation. Over-rejecting every absence claim to turn CM-CL3-03 green is forbidden by PC-CL3-01.

obligations.proposition: Every limitation code emitted by v1 is classified informational vs obligation-degrading, and every obligation-degrading code reaches the gate through a consumed artifact.
obligations.mechanism_site: plan-level restatement (semantic_chunker) or explicit gate input; manifest/brief are not consumed today
obligations.closure_predicate: classification table committed; one test per degrading class at gate level

v1_v2_isolation.regression_gate: NORMATIVE (procedural): both CI jobs must be green on the exact HEAD: `Validate repository` (ci.yml, runs scripts/test.sh = full suite minus integration/requires_runtime/requires_docker/requires_prometheus/requires_network markers) and `AgentReview release gates` (ci.yml, runs scripts/ci_validate.sh: section 8 same selection, section 9 the requires_network tests, which include v2 content-extraction/redaction E2E, diff acquisition, transport, isolated executor and trusted-check tests). GitHub enforces nothing here: master has required_status_checks=null, required_pull_request_reviews=null and no rulesets (observed 2026-09-30), so this gate is enforced by the campaign's PRE_MERGE_GATE, not by the forge. gate_unavailable on GitHub runners (non-root): v2 tests that skip without root, sudo broker, unprivileged user namespaces, casefold tmpfs, POSIX ACLs, inotify or mknod (test_c3_focal_obligations, test_isolated_executor_v2, test_physical_snapshot_v2, test_target_pack_epoch*_v2, test_trusted_*_v2). A slice that changes a shared_v1_owned path must additionally run the full suite locally and report which of those tests ran or skipped; it may not claim them as passed. A local v1 subset is iteration convenience only. CI IDENTITY: both jobs check out the pull_request default ref, i.e. the synthetic merge commit refs/pull/<n>/merge, not the head SHA. CI evidence binds to the exact HEAD only if that merge commit's tree equals the head tree; PRE_MERGE_GATE fetches `pull/<n>/merge` and compares `<merge>^{tree}` with `<head>^{tree}` (unequal = evidence does not bind; STOP_PRE_MERGE_GATE_FAILED). V1-C0 at 69a8d4b0: merge parents ab92e89f + 69a8d4b0, merge tree == head tree == ff7d703a.
v1_v2_isolation.collection_preservation: NORMATIVE (procedural): the slice PR records `pytest --collect-only -q` node IDs under the CI marker selection on base and head; any node ID present on base and absent on head is STOP unless the task contract names it. Changed or added test files must not define `pytest_plugins` or `pytest_*` hook functions. This closes test-selection tampering (e.g. a test module registering itself as a plugin to deselect v2 tests), which the file-level scope check cannot see.
v1_v2_isolation.residual_limitation: v1/v2 isolation is NOT statically proven. It is carried by positive write scope (C1), policy immutability (C2), no new v2 dependency (C3), shared-path justification (C4), collection preservation, the full-suite regression_gate (behavioral, bounded by existing v2 test coverage and runner gate_unavailable tests) and independent review of each slice diff. A change to a v1_exclusive module that alters v2 behavior through an existing undetected path and no v2 test would not be caught.
v1_v2_isolation.principle: isolation rests on positive write scope and behavioral full-suite evidence; no v1/v2 classifier of the tree carries the gate (every classifier attempted in review proved incomplete)
v1_v2_isolation.executable_checker_removed: An executable scope checker (evidence/v1_scope_check.py) was prototyped in this slice and removed after five consecutive post-READY Codex rounds each found a new P2 in it (scope self-expansion, module-form references, fnmatch '/' crossing, self-modification of its own guard, false-blocking of admissible tests, missed v1->v2 imports). A bespoke static checker became its own unbounded verification surface inside a contract-only slice. The obligations it tried to enforce are kept as the deterministic git commands in procedural_checks; static detection of v1->v2 reach through existing code is not claimed (see residual_limitation).
